engine.meaning: The release is reproduced almost verbatim, so every fact survives: "one of three F-5 fighter jets", "from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT", "Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8".
engine.sense: The one slang swap misfires: "connect the agency with the punters, technologies, and organisations" turns the people who drive space leadership into customers or gamblers.
engine.authenticity: Apart from spelling ("organisations", "honour") and "punters", it is unchanged US press-release prose: "NASA team members will engage with fans at the agency’s Experience Zone".
engine.register: Far under level 4: effectively untranslated, e.g. "NASA’s Inspiration Tour convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders".
engine.tone: The upbeat promotional tone is the original's, unchanged.
engine.flow: Reads as the original release; "the punters, technologies, and organisations" is the only jolt.

unharnessed.meaning: All facts kept: "one of three F-5 fighter jets", "from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT", "Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8", "250th birthday". Added asides are colour: "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh?", "wraps up with a bang".
unharnessed.sense: Most terms fit: "at the stick of", "having a yarn with the fans", "have a crack at some interactive games", "happy snaps", "public sector mob", "shindig". "start the footy" stretches "footy" to American football, which Australians would call gridiron.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural ("grab a few happy snaps with a bloody big inflatable SLS"), but "is gonna be at the stick" is American, and the tag "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh?" is a stock aside.
unharnessed.register: A full level-4 retelling of a press release, with dad-level "bloody big"; on brief.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the upbeat, promotional energy, now matey: "the multi-day, family-friendly shindig will show off the next-generation aircraft".
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "With stops right across the country, NASA's Inspiration Tour rounds up the academic, industry and public sector mob to hook the agency up with the people".
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "at the stick", "footy", "having a yarn", "Punters", "have a crack", "happy snaps", "mob", "hook ... up", "shindig", "getting about".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the NASA flyover announcement, all four paragraphs in order.

yarn.meaning: All facts kept, with a gloss: "NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, the agency's top boss", "from 10am to 1pm EDT", "Saturday 7 November and Sunday 8 November". The "gridiron game" gloss is helpful colour.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "at the controls", "having a yarn with fans", "have a crack at hands-on games", "a big blow-up SLS", "gridiron game", "getting about".
yarn.authenticity: Natural Australian newsroom English: "New York Jets v Cleveland Browns gridiron game", "snap photos with a big blow-up SLS (Space Launch System) rocket".
yarn.register: Lighter than level 4: a well-localised news piece with a few touches ("having a yarn", "have a crack", "blow-up") rather than a matey retelling; the last two paragraphs are close to plain prose.
yarn.tone: Keeps the promotional tone: "show off the next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, driverless vehicles and technologies".
yarn.flow: Smooth; the restructured first sentence reads well.
yarn.variety: Some range: "top boss", "having a yarn", "have a crack", "blow-up", "players", "getting about".
